text:
sasha: ran a long nsys + perfetto trace on the 8xA100 serving config this morning. timeline shows a ton of tiny kernels around the kv-cache path and one dominant fused_flash_attn_v2 kernel occupying GPU timelots. attaching snippets below.

emily: can you paste the nsys command you used? also did you capture user ranges?

sasha: ran: ```nsys profile --trace=cuda,cublas,cudnn --sample=none -o run_kv_v2 nsys_out ./serve_bench --model gpt-7b --seq 2048 --batch 4 --requests 2000``` captured cpuslice + cuda ranges. perfetto was exported via nsys convert.

rahul: quick take: that many small kernels around KV read/write usually points to per-token kernel launches for kv read, not coalesced reads. could be due to our kernel-selection falling back to scalar read for certain seq lengths.

sasha: exact timeline excerpt (perfetto flame): 
```
0.0s  fused_flash_attn_v2   42% GPU
0.5s  kv_read_kernel_part1 8%
0.55s kv_read_kernel_part2 6%
0.62s kv_write_hook 10% (lots of stall waits)
0.75s small_pointwise_x 12% (many launches)
```

emily: nvprof reported high L2 miss rate on the kv read buffers? did you get memory counters?

sasha: yes — nvprof/metrics: dram_read_throughput moderate but l2_read_miss_rate ~ 36% on kv read, and sm_efficiency dips when kv_write happens.

perf-bot: :warning: PERF_REGRESSION_ALERT: ServeLatency p50 increased by 12% on canary vs baseline at 2026-02-14T09:12Z. Trace id: run_kv_v2.

marco: interesting — the fused_flash_attn_v2 kernel is big but constant. The regression looks correlated with increased kv_write syncs we introduced in 2 commits ago (the eager-kv-flush). Could the new kv flush path be serializing streams?

rahul: i checked the CUDA streams ordering in the trace — kv_write_hook is submitted to stream 1, attention kernels to stream 0, but there's an explicit cudaStreamSynchronize() right after kv_write_hook in the runtime if fallback_kv_enabled=false. that would force a sync and fragment execution.

emily: if that's true, we should try two quick experiments: (1) disable eager-kv-flush and run nsys for 500 requests to see if p50 drops; (2) try increasing microbatch size so kv read/writes amortize across threads.

sasha: queued both experiments. preliminary run with eager-kv-flush off shows p50 down ~9% and much fewer small kernel launches — perfetto shows the kv path coalesced into 2 kernels rather than 8.

marco: good. but note the fused_flash_attn_v2 still takes majority time. we should test alternate kernel selection: try fused_flash_attn_smallseq fallback for seq<64 and flash_variant for seq>=64. the runtime currently picks flash_variant heuristically by seqBuckets; might be misclassifying because of padding.

rahul: also saw L2 miss contours change when we enabled fused_kv_read. enabling it reduced L2 misses to ~12%. suggestion: add a quick runtime toggle to prefer coalesced_kv_read when batch_token_count > threshold.

emily: action items: 
- sasha: run A/B traces (eager-kv-flush on/off) and attach perfetto full timelines (keep raw nsys .qdrep)
- rahul: patch runtime to gate eager-kv-flush behind stream-safe async write (no sync) and add metric for per-request kernel count
- marco: add a kernel-selection flag to experiment with flash variants and log chosen kernel id in trace user ranges

sasha: will upload traces to /internal/trace-archive/run_kv_v2_qdrep and paste links when done. early logs: 
```
[2026-03-16T08:12:03Z] p50: 48ms (canary with eager-flush)
[2026-03-16T08:30:11Z] p50: 44ms (eager-flush off)
```

perf-bot: :white_check_mark: regression partially mitigated on canary. New p50 within acceptable delta. Continue with kernel selection experiments.

emily: one more note — perfetto slices show small_pointwise_x kernels are launching because we sometimes compile per-head pointwise for certain dims. could cache compiled kernels keyed by head_size to avoid repeated JITs.

rahul: good call. caching would reduce launch overhead. i'll prototype a simple head_size->kernel cache and run microbenchmarks.

marco: thanks everyone. let's keep traces small but reproducible. if anyone is debugging offline ping me and i can repro with a host that matches the canary infra. :coffee:
